decisionsTitle: The birth date is typed day first, and the words under it are its helper
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-09-29 13:45**, a screenshot of the registration form's «Data nașterii *» box: «Aici am un overlap urât la drop-down». The screenshot showed two defects. The date in words of §467 («Vineri, 11 mai 1990 · 36 de ani în ziua evenimentului») was drawn over the box's bottom outline: it was a separate line pulled up by a negative margin, and the crowding §546 answered by removing the helper sentence came back through the echo itself. And the box read «05/11/1990» for 11 May: the browser's own `<input type="date">` draws the digits in the browser's order, month first on an English-language phone, and no attribute a page can set changes that — the defect §439 fixed for the time box, against §345's rule that every date the platform shows reads day first.

**Decision (amending §467, applying §345's order to the public form).** The birth date on the public registration form and on the desk's «Înscriere nouă» is one island, `BirthDateField`: a typed text box that shows the date as the backoffice's picker shows it, `DATE_DISPLAY_FORMAT` (`11.05.1990`, «ZZ.LL.AAAA» / «DD.MM.YYYY» as its placeholder), and reads it day first in both languages — «05/11/1990», «5.11.1990», «05-11-1990», «05 11 1990» and «05111990» (a phone's numeric keypad has no dot) are all 5 November. On leaving the box it shows `05.11.1990`. It posts `YYYY-MM-DD` as before: the server reads the typed text through the same function (`normalizeTypedDate` in `form-mapping.ts` and in the desk's action), so a browser without JavaScript, whose `pattern` accepts the same shapes, posts what it typed and is read the same. The date in words is now the field's own `FormHelperText`, under the outline with every helper's margin, computed from the same reading the box posts — the two can never disagree. The bounds the server applies (a hundred and twenty years back; the youngest birth date that is the event's minimum age on the race day) are the input's custom validity, set in the keystroke's handler, so the browser refuses first and the «Mai lipsesc:» list (§422) names the box. `GuardianForMinor`, `HiddenForMinor` and the desk read the box through the same `readTypedDate`.

**Refused.** The backoffice's MUI picker on the public form: §345 keeps the picker and its date library off every public page (`pickers-backoffice-only.test.ts`), and a birth date decades back is faster typed than paged to. The box shares the backoffice's format and module (`shared/forms/pickers/wall-values.ts`, which imports nothing), not its component — one display rule, no second configuration. The brief's slash order «ZZ/LL/AAAA» was not taken: the backoffice shows dots, and the same format everywhere was the point; the slash is still read. `BR-REQ-050-02` criterion 36 ("it stays the browser's own date box") is amended: never the picker still holds, the browser's date box no longer does.

**Under the minimum age, the box says the rule (the owner, 2026-09-29 13:50).** With a birth date under the event's minimum age (§321, §329) the box went red, but the only words under it were the date in words («Luni, 11 mai 2020 · 6 ani în ziua evenimentului») — «ar trebui să văd și mesajul de eroare că nu am vârsta minimă». Now, as soon as a whole date under the minimum is typed, the helper shows the rule first, in the error colour — the summary's own sentence for this box (§47), «Vârsta minimă de participare la acest eveniment este 14 ani împliniți în ziua cursei.», with the event's own minimum, never typed — and the date in words with the age it gives under it. After the server's refusal the box reads the same way, until the person types in it again; then the live verdict answers, so a corrected date is not still called wrong. A half-typed date says nothing: «11.05» is unfinished, not refused. The «Mai lipsesc:» list names «Data nașterii» from the same custom validity. No word was added to the catalogues for it.
changelogLine: - **The birth date reads day first, and the words under it no longer overlap the box** — «05/11/1990» is 5 November in both languages on the registration form and the desk, the box shows `05.11.1990` as the backoffice does, the date in words sits under the box as its helper, and a date under the event's minimum age says the rule in red as it is typed. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the public registration form or the desk's new registration, when a birth date is typed, then it is read day first in both languages — «05/11/1990», «5.11.1990», «05-11-1990», «05 11 1990» and «05111990» are 5 November 1990 — the box shows it as `05.11.1990` on leaving it, with «ZZ.LL.AAAA» / «DD.MM.YYYY» as its placeholder, and the form posts `1990-11-05`; a browser without JavaScript posts the typed text and the server reads it the same (2026-09-29, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 23. The birth date in words, with the age on the event's day, is the birth-date box's own helper text, under its outline and never drawn over it, and it always names the same day the box posts (2026-09-29, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a whole birth date under the event's minimum age N on the race day, when it is typed, then the box turns red and its helper shows, first, the refusal summary's own sentence with N from the event — «Vârsta minimă de participare la acest eveniment este N ani împliniți în ziua cursei.» / «The minimum age for this event is N years on the day of the race.» — and the date in words with its age under it; the «Mai lipsesc:» list names «Data nașterii»; after the server's refusal the helper reads the same until the box is typed in again (2026-09-29, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 36. Given a birth date — the public registration form's or the staff form's — when the form renders, then it is a typed text box shown in the backoffice picker's own format, `DD.MM.YYYY`, never the browser's date box and never the backoffice picker, and the public form never loads the picker (2026-09-29, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the birth date reads day first, with its words and the minimum-age rule under the box
